messages.text: What is eye diagram, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?

The knowledge base gave no validated answer; evidence was insufficient for a complete product/option recommendation. It did return partial evidence connecting **eye diagram** to signal-integrity measurement workflows and PCIe eye-opening decisions.

**Not from the knowledge base — general definition:**  
An **eye diagram** is an oscilloscope-style visualization made by overlaying many bits or symbols of a high-speed digital signal on top of each other. The open area in the middle looks like an “eye.” Its **height** and **width** show how much timing and voltage margin the signal has. A more open eye usually means better signal integrity; a closed or distorted eye suggests jitter, noise, inter-symbol interference, loss, crosstalk, skew, or insufficient equalization.

From the partial knowledge-base evidence, understanding eye diagrams affects these product-related measurement decisions:

| Decision area | Why eye-diagram understanding matters |
|---|---|
| **PCIe redriver / high-speed link validation** | PCIe redriver output requirements can be expressed as required **eye opening**, including eye height and eye width after equalization. |
| **High-speed PCB/PCBA signal-integrity test flow** | Eye diagram is treated as a standard SI measurement item alongside insertion loss, crosstalk, TDR impedance, stackup planning, and transmission-line calculation. |
| **PCB material and stackup selection** | R&S PCB test-solution material/stackup workflows include items such as IL, Dk/Df, roughness, impedance, crosstalk, transmission-line modeling, and eye diagram. |
| **Skew and fiber-weave investigation** | Intra-pair skew from fiberglass/epoxy dielectric differences can degrade the receiver’s differential eye diagram, so the eye helps decide whether skew needs deeper analysis. |
| **Whether time-domain analysis capability is needed** | The returned evidence mentioned “extended time domain analysis including eye diagram,” but did not validate a specific model or option code. |
| **Cable/connector evidence quality** | For high-speed cables/connectors, lack of eye-diagram, BER, or compliance evidence weakens product claims. |

Key limitation: the knowledge base did **not** validate a formal product recommendation, named instrument model, option code, standard, fixture, or calibration method for eye-diagram measurement.

data.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

### Short answer
The passages do not give a formal definition of an eye diagram; they treat **Eye diagram** as a high-speed PCB/PCBA signal-integrity measurement item alongside IL/Xtalk, TDR impedance, stackup planning, and transmission-line calculation, and they quantify related **eye opening** by eye height and eye width after equalization in PCIe context [19][21][7].
### Product-related measurement decisions that depend on it
| Measurement decision | What the passages support |
|---|---|
| Decide whether a PCIe redriver output meets eye-opening requirements | PCIe redriver output eye opening must be greater than or equal to the listed eye-opening values, and the listed metrics are extrapolated eye height after EQ and minimum eye width after EQ, measured post-equalization before 3-tap DFE blocks [7]. |
| Decide what to include in high-speed PCB/PCBA signal-integrity flow | The signal-integrity flow of high-speed PCB/PCBA explicitly includes IL / Xtalk / Eye diagram, plus TDR impedance, stackup planner, and TL calculator [19][21]. |
| Decide material/stackup-selection measurement coverage for PCB fabricator or system house workflows | R&S PCB test solutions list Material/Stackup selection items as IL, DK/DF, roughness, impedance, Xtalk, TL modeling, and Eye diagram [22][24]. |
| Decide whether fiber-weave skew or intra-pair skew must be investigated because it affects the received differential eye | Fiberglass/epoxy dielectric differences can make differential-pair signals experience different velocities, causing intra-pair skew and degrading the receiver’s differential eye diagram [8]. |
| Decide whether an “Extended time domain analysis” capability is relevant when eye-diagram analysis is needed | The raw source lists “Extended time domain analysis (including eye diagram),” but the passages do not provide a product model or option code for that capability [98][85]. |
| Decide whether high-speed cable/connector product claims have enough measurement evidence | Some product-related sources explicitly lack eye-diagram evidence, including Direct Attached Copper Cables lacking cable length, gauge, BER, eye diagram, active/passive boundary, power, compliance, order number, or customer evidence, and Celerity 224 Gb/s BGA Mezzanine Connectors lacking PAM4 eye diagram, BER, compliance, or datasheet version [25][28]. |
### Key limitation
The passages connect eye diagram to measurement flows and requirements, but they do not provide a formal eye-diagram definition, named instrument model, option code, order number, test standard, fixture, or calibration method for eye-diagram measurement [80][81][85].
